ja: 梅田綾香は1993年広島県生まれで、蝋染めで制作しています。
今回の個展のタイトルは「emerge」です。
彼女は、蝋染めならではの世界を追求しています。
一枚の布に現れる現象から、断片、システム、そして世界へと広がっていきます。
レヴィ=ストロースの構造主義と「ブリコラージュ」の考え方を参照しています。
染料は動き、にじみ、蝋をはじくので、結果を完全には制御できません。
最後に蝋を落とすので、制作過程の痕跡は表面に残りません。
この展覧会で彼女は再び現象から始め、世界を立ち上がらせます。
2025年に「Inaudible Orchestra」を発表しました。
2024年に「空洞と瞬き(Hollow and Blink)」を発表しました。
2023年に銀座のGallery Seekで個展「花隠れ(Last Flowers)」を開催しました。
2022年に「多元的ビオトープ」を発表しました。
テーマはシリーズごと、時系列で少しずつ変化しています。
原田武は1984年愛知県生まれで、広島県安芸高田市に住んでいます。
虫やカエル、植物などの小さな生き物を金属で作っています。
テーマは「郷愁」です。
子供の頃に自然を夢中で観察して感じた喜びを再構築しています。
写実が目的ではなく、記憶をたどるうちに自然と生まれると語っています。
技術を見せるのではなく、バランスと余白で空気感を表現します。
岡﨑実央は1995年札幌生まれで、武蔵野美術大学を卒業しました。
プロレスをキュビズムの手法で描いています。
観客はリングを360度取り囲み、席ごとに見え方が違います。
そのすべての視点を一枚の絵に収めています。
以前は週刊プロレスの編集部で働いていました。
プロレスを知らずに通り過ぎるのはもったいないので、作品でその魅力を紹介したいと語っています。
Sizzleは東京在住の画家で、独学で絵を学び2022年に活動を始めました。
主題は「視覚言語」です。
認知科学の「イメージスキーマ」の考え方を絵画に応用しています。
あいまいな情報に意味を見出す人間の心理(無意識の投影)も取り入れています。
具体的なモチーフを避けるので、鑑賞者ごとに違う体験が生まれます。
古川千夏は純銀の素地に七宝を制作しています。
通常この技法では、銀線は研磨で消えてしまいます。
彼女はあえて突出させ、線を境界ではなく主役にしています。
わずかに浮いた線がやわらかな陰影を生み、光や角度で表情が変わります。

en: Ayaka Umeda was born in Hiroshima in 1993 and works with batik, the wax-resist dyeing technique.
This exhibition is called emerge.
She pursues a world that only wax-resist dyeing can create.
From a phenomenon that appears on a single cloth, to fragments, to a system, and then to a world.
She draws on the structuralism of Claude Levi-Strauss and his idea of bricolage.
Dye moves, bleeds, and resists the wax, so the result can never be fully controlled.
At the end, the wax is removed, so the process leaves no visible trace on the surface.
With this show, she starts again from the phenomenon and lets a world emerge.
In 2025, she presented Inaudible Orchestra.
In 2024, she presented Hollow and Blink.
In 2023, she held a solo exhibition called Last Flowers at Gallery Seek in Ginza.
In 2022, she presented Multidimensional Biotope.
Her themes have changed with each series over time.
Takeshi Harada was born in Aichi in 1984 and lives in Akitakata, Hiroshima.
He makes small living things, such as insects, frogs, and plants, out of metal.
His theme is nostalgia.
He recreates the joy he felt as a child, watching nature with great curiosity.
He says realism is not the goal. It comes naturally as he recalls his memories.
He does not show off technique. He expresses the air of a work through balance and empty space.
Mio Okazaki was born in Sapporo in 1995 and graduated from Musashino Art University.
She paints pro wrestling in the style of Cubism.
Fans surround the ring from 360 degrees, and each seat has a different view.
She puts all those views into one painting.
She used to work for Weekly Pro Wrestling magazine.
She says it would be a waste to pass by without knowing pro wrestling, so her art is her way of introducing it.
Sizzle is a painter based in Tokyo. She taught herself to paint and began her career in 2022.
Her theme is visual language.
She applies the idea of image schema from cognitive science to painting.
She also draws on the human tendency to project meaning onto vague information.
She avoids concrete motifs, so every viewer can have a different experience.
Chinatsu Furukawa makes cloisonne, called shippo in Japanese, on pure silver.
Usually, the silver wire is polished away in this technique.
She leaves it standing out on purpose, so the line becomes the main subject, not just a border.
The slightly raised lines create soft shadows, and the look changes with the light and the angle.

Q: What is the exhibition emerge about?
A: It is Ayaka Umeda's exhibition. She starts again from a phenomenon on the cloth, and lets a world emerge from it.

Q: What is batik?
A: It is a technique of drawing with wax on cloth, and then dyeing it. The wax keeps the dye out, so the dye only colors the parts without wax.

Q: Can the artist control the colors?
A: Not completely. The dye moves and bleeds on its own, and she works with that movement.

Q: Did the artist use paint?
A: No paint at all. All the colors come from the metal itself, chemical reactions, and heating with a flame.

Q: How is the metal shaped?
A: He hammers a metal sheet into shape, and joins the parts with welding or silver solder. It is not cast in a mold.

Q: Can I really use this incense burner?
A: Yes, you can burn incense in it. The design is subtle, so you may not notice at first. That is part of the charm.

Q: Will the metal change color over time?
A: It has a coating, so it will not change quickly. Over a long time it may dull a little, but the color can be restored.

Q: Do I need to know pro wrestling to enjoy this?

Q: Why does she use Cubism?
A: In pro wrestling, fans surround the ring, and each seat has a different view. Cubism lets her put all those views into one painting.

Q: Does she paint any sports besides wrestling?

Q: Is this an abstract painting?
A: You can call it abstract, because it has no concrete motif. But the artist sees it as a kind of visual language.

Q: What is image schema?
A: It is a concept from cognitive science. It means basic patterns of thought that we get from our body experience. For example, the idea of a container.

Q: What tools did the artist use?
A: She uses a painting knife and a stapler. You can see the marks of those tools on the surface.

Q: Does the artist do live painting?
A: Yes. She has done live painting at events and on walls. Let me check if it is possible for you.

Q: What is cloisonne?
A: It is a technique of firing glass-like glaze onto metal. She uses pure silver, and fires it at about 800 degrees Celsius.

Q: What is different about her work?
A: Usually the silver wire is polished away. She leaves it standing out, so the line becomes the main subject.

Q: Does the artist make the metal base herself?
A: Yes. She hammers the base, joins the parts, and does the wires, the glaze, and the firing all by herself.

Q: How should I hang this on my wall?
A: The lighting changes how it looks. Direct light shows the surface texture, and natural light brings out the sparkle of the silver. Let me help you choose the spot.

A: The lighting changes how it looks. Direct light shows the surface texture, and natural light brings out the sparkle of the silver. Let me help you choose the spot.
